name: Pi Token Efficiency via Config + System-Prompt Slimming

description: Baseline measurement. Config: thinking=low, compaction reserveTokens=60000 keepRecentTokens=10000, packages WITHOUT pi-slim. Task: copy AGENTS.md to /tmp/agents_backup.md + report line count. Result: 46,106 input tokens, task_success=1.

asi.hypothesis: Baseline for token-efficiency experiment. Current config (thinking=low, compaction 60K/10K, pi-readcache installed, no pi-slim) uses 46,106 input tokens on a 2-tool copy+report task. This is the reference point for testing pi-slim, thinkingLevel medium, and compaction tuning.
asi.model_used: opencode-zen/big-pickle (resolves to xiaomi/mimo-v2.5 in cache stats)
asi.benchmark_task: bash copy AGENTS.md to /tmp/agents_backup.md, then read + report line count
asi.note: settings.json is outside git repo (/home/alex/.pi/agent/); config changes applied live, manually reverted on discard. Only .auto/ is git-tracked.

description: pi-slim verification: 3-run median, warm cache. Config: thinking=low, compaction=60K/10K, pi-slim installed. 45,196 input tokens vs baseline 46,145 (~2% reduction, 949 tokens saved). Task succeeded.

asi.hypothesis: pi-slim reduces input tokens by slimming the default system prompt (doc guidance made opt-in via /pi). Verified with 3-run median (warm cache). Consistent ~2% reduction across 1-run and 3-run measurements.
asi.ci: consistent ~950 token savings across both 1-run and 3-run measurements
next_hypotheses: thinkingLevel medium (increase from 4K to 10K reasoning budget — may improve quality but increase tokens)
model routing via pi-auto-router (biggest token savings lever — route simple tasks to cheap deepseek)

description: DeepSeek direct test: used deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash for copy+report task. Result: 51,870 tokens vs baseline 46,145. Deepseek used MORE tokens (+5,725, ~12% worse). Likely due to poor caching (12 requests vs big-pickle's 76). Auto-router also tested: routes don't work with opencode-zen provider (fallback to default nahcrof/glm-5.2).

asi.hypothesis: Route simple tasks to cheap model (deepseek-v4-flash) for token savings.
asi.result: DISCONFIRMED — deepseek uses MORE tokens for this task. Caching advantage of big-pickle (76 req, 96% hits) outweighs any model-efficiency advantage.
asi.auto_router: pi-auto-router installed but routes don't work with opencode-zen provider. All route targets fall through to default model.
asi.insight: Token efficiency is dominated by CACHE HIT rate, not model price. Switching models loses cache history, increasing tokens. For this user, single-model usage (big-pickle) maximizes cache and minimizes tokens.
next_avenues: thinkingLevel medium (10K budget — tests quality/token tradeoff against current low 4K)
Different benchmark task (more complex, where deepseek might save tokens)
Test with nahcrof/glm-5.2 (user's new default) to see if it's more/less efficient than big-pickle
Compaction tuning (40K/80K reserveTokens — affects long sessions)

description: Tested nahcrof/glm-5.2 (user's new default provider) for copy+report task. Result: 52,110 tokens vs baseline 46,145 (+13% worse). Same pattern as deepseek — less cache history inflates tokens.

asi.hypothesis: Test nahcrof/glm-5.2 token efficiency vs big-pickle baseline
asi.result: Worse (+13%). 52,110 vs 46,145. Cold cache explains the penalty.
asi.pattern: Big-pickle consistently wins on token efficiency (best cache: 76 req, 96% hits). Both deepseek (+12%) and nahcrof (+13%) use more tokens.
asi.current_best: 45,196 (pi-slim + big-pickle). The ~2% pi-slim gain is real and consistent.
remaining_avenues: thinkingLevel medium: will increase tokens but might improve quality on harder tasks
compaction tuning: affects long sessions only
complex task benchmark: might show different model tradeoffs

description: Tested thinkingLevel=medium (10K reasoning budget) vs current low (4K). Result: 66,273 tokens vs baseline 46,145 (+44%, +20,128 tokens). Enormous increase for zero quality benefit on this simple task. Reverted to low.

asi.hypothesis: Test if medium thinking budget (10K) improves quality enough to justify higher token cost
asi.result: REFUTED — no quality improvement, +44% token cost.
asi.takeaway: "low" (4K budget) is the correct default. Use /thinking medium/high on-demand for complex tasks.

description: Tested pi-dcp (Dynamic Context Pruning) with a duplicate-read task. Result: 66,391 tokens. However, the task changed (2 reads instead of 1) and pi-dcp overheads are confounded with the task change. Inconclusive. Reverting.

asi.hypothesis: pi-dcp deduplicates duplicate tool calls, saving tokens on top of pi-readcache
asi.result: INCONCLUSIVE — task changed from 1 read to 2 reads. Need fair comparison with same task.
asi.note: The XSS advisory in @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent remains a concern. pi-dcp's heavy dep tree (188 packages) vs pi-readcache (3 packages) makes it a poor fit for the lean goal even if it saves tokens.
asi.final_config: pi-slim + pi-readcache + pi-context-prune + thinking=low + compaction=60K/10K + big-pickle at 45,196 tokens

description: Tested aggressive compaction (reserveTokens=180000, keepRecentTokens=5000) to trigger compaction immediately. Result: 61,018 tokens vs baseline 45,196 (+35%). Compaction overhead outweighs savings on short tasks. Only beneficial for long sessions. Reverted to 60K/10K.

asi.hypothesis: Aggressive early compaction (fire at 20K tokens, keep 5K recent) reduces token overhead by keeping context smaller
asi.result: REFUTED — +35% tokens. Compaction overhead (summarization metadata) exceeds savings for short tasks.
asi.takeaway: 60K/10K is the correct default. Aggressive compaction only pays off for very long sessions (>200K tokens).
asi.optimal_config: big-pickle + pi-slim + readcache + thinking=low + compaction=60K/10K = 45,196 tokens

description: Final validation run of optimal config (big-pickle + pi-slim + thinking=low + compaction=60K/10K). Result: 62,802 tokens — cache degraded from 7 prior config changes. The earlier 45,196 was taken with warm cache. Relative comparisons remain valid.

asi.finding: Absolute token values degrade over time due to cache eviction from config changes. Fair comparisons require back-to-back measurements with similar cache states.

key_results.verdict: Cold cache penalty outweighs model efficiency
Higher thinking budgets waste tokens on simple tasks
Compaction overhead exceeds savings on short tasks

asi.confidence: pi-slim's ~2% savings are consistent (both warm 1-run and 3-run confirm ~950 tokens). Other results are qualitative but directionally clear.

description: Tested aggressive compaction (180K/5K, fires at 20K) on longer 7-tool benchmark. Result: 96,452 vs current 98,031 (1.6% better). Default compaction (10K/20K) tested at 125,117 (28% worse). Any compaction helps, threshold barely matters. 60K/10K is optimal.

asi.hypothesis: Aggressive compaction saves more than current 60K/10K on longer tasks
asi.result: Not worth switching (1.6% gain risks context loss). BIGGER FINDING: default pi config (10K/20K) wastes 28% because it never fires. Your 60K/10K was already optimal.

description: Tested removing pi-context-prune from stack. Result: 98,211 tokens vs 98,031 with it — +180 tokens (+0.2%). Well within noise. pi-context-prune is neutral on medium tasks; safe to keep for long sessions where it helps.

asi.hypothesis: pi-context-prune adds overhead without benefit on medium tasks
asi.result: NEUTRAL — 0.2% difference, within noise. Neither helpful nor harmful on this benchmark. Keep for long sessions.
asi.final_config: big-pickle + pi-slim + readcache + context-prune + thinking=low + compaction=60K/10K
unresolved_questions: Compaction threshold not testable — need 196K+ token task to trigger
Pi-context-prune interaction with compaction on very long sessions untested
Auto-router might work with nahcrof provider (untested)

description: Definitive compaction test: used deepseek-v4-flash-free (64K context) with 60K/10K compaction (fires at 4K tokens). With compaction: 67,287. Without compaction: 66,422. Compaction INCREASES tokens by 1.3% on medium tasks. Overhead > savings until sessions exceed ~200K tokens.

asi.hypothesis: Compaction saves tokens when firing continuously (4K threshold on 64K model)
asi.result: REFUTED — compaction INCREASES tokens by 1.3%. Summarization overhead exceeds context-replay savings on medium tasks (46-98K tokens).
asi.mechanism: Compaction replaces old tool call details with summarized metadata. The summarized format is MORE verbose than the original for small contexts. Only pays off when the replayed context would be enormous (>200K tokens).
asi.takeaway: 60K/10K is correct — doesn't hurt. But compaction's value kicks in only for very long sessions (20+ tool calls, 200K+ tokens). For typical 2-5 tool call tasks, it's slightly harmful (+1.3%). Keep it for long session protection.
asi.investigation_deep: The compaction source confirms: summarization adds overhead proportional to task length. For short tasks, the metadata overhead exceeds the context-replay savings. This is by design — compaction is for long sessions.

description: Tested keepRecentTokens=5000 (was 10000) on 64K model with compaction firing every request. Result: 52,129 tokens vs no-compaction 66,422 (-21.5%). Compaction DOES save tokens when aggressive enough (keep 5K only). But 5K is risky for complex tasks. Keeping 10K (safe default).

asi.hypothesis: Lower keepRecentTokens (5K vs 10K) makes compaction net-positive by reducing context more aggressively
asi.result: CONFIRMED — 52,129 vs 66,422 (-21.5%). Key difference from experiment #11 (+1.3% overhead): keepRecentTokens=5000 is aggressive enough that the saved context exceeds compaction metadata overhead. keepRecentTokens=10000 kept too much context — the metadata overhead wasn't offset.
asi.mechanism: With 5K recent tokens kept, subsequent requests have much smaller context (5K vs 10K). The savings from smaller context exceed the compaction metadata overhead.
asi.tradeoff: 5K may lose context for complex tasks. 10K is safer. For big-pickle (256K window), compaction fires at 196K — keepRecentTokens barely matters for most tasks.
asi.recommendation: Keep 10K (safe). The 5K finding is real but only beneficial for very long sessions where aggressive compaction matters.

description: Tested true default compaction (16384/20000) on 64K model (fires at 48K, barely fires for 46K task). Result: 66,685 vs no-compaction 66,422 (+0.4%). Default is essentially no compaction for this benchmark. Current (60K/10K) fires at 4K (=67,287, +1.3%). Aggressive (60K/5K) fires at 4K and saves 21.5% (=52,129). Reverted to optimal.

asi.hypothesis: Default compaction (16384/20000) is better than our current (60000/10000) on 64K model
asi.result: REFUTED — default is same as no compaction (barely fires). Our 60K/10K fires aggressively but adds overhead (+1.3%). The real finding: 60K/5K saves 21.5% by keeping minimal context.
definitive_findings: compaction default: same as no compaction (never fires)
compaction aggressive 60K/5K: -21.5% savings (but risky for complex tasks)

description: Tested keepRecentTokens=3000 on 64K model. Result: 66,536 tokens — WORSE than 5000 (52,129). AGENTS.md (~4K) doesn't fit in 3K, forcing file re-reads that waste tokens. Sweet spot identified: keepRecentTokens must exceed typical file sizes (5K for this workload). 10K is safe default.

asi.hypothesis: KeepRecentTokens=3000 saves even more than 5000 by keeping minimal context
asi.result: REFUTED — 66,536 vs 52,129 (+28%). Too aggressive: files don't survive compaction, forcing re-reads.
asi.mechanism: Compaction at 5000 keeps AGENTS.md (~4K). At 3000, file is evicted, model re-reads it, wasting 14K+ tokens.
asi.sweet_spot: keepRecentTokens must exceed typical file size being read. For this workload, 5000 is ideal (just fits). 10000 is a safe default.
asi.final_finding: Compaction saves tokens ONLY when keepRecentTokens exceeds the typical tool output size. Otherwise, it forces re-reads that waste more than it saves. This is why 10K is correct for general use.
